subject: SLA exception request — Cyneris private deployment & customer KMS
messages:
From: Dana Mills <dana@cyneris-health.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@cyneris-health.com
Date: Mon, 18 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Request: SLA coverage for private deployment with customer-managed KMS

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're progressing through procurement and security review, but our compliance team flagged the SLA language for the private (VPC) deployment. Cyneris will be hosting the HSM/KMS and managing the on-prem gateways; as a result we cannot accept a standard availability SLA that attributes outages caused by our key management or WAN to Redwood.

Two asks from our side:
- Can Redwood provide an addendum that excludes customer-managed KMS and last-mile WAN from uptime calculations, and outlines evidence we can provide during incident review?
- If Redwood cannot fully exclude those components, can we get a clearly scoped exception (e.g., network/KMS carve-out with a 99.5% availability target for the Redwood-managed portion)?

We need an answer for the procurement committee by EOD Friday so please let me know if you need anything from our infra team.

Attachments: none

Thanks,
Dana Mills
VP Ops, Cyneris Health
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Dana Mills <dana@cyneris-health.com>
Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 Oct 2027 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA coverage for private deployment with customer-managed KMS

Hi Dana —

Appreciate the clear ask and timeline. We've reviewed internally and sketched a conservative approach that should address procurement and security while preserving our operational guarantees. High level:

- Proposal: "SLA Addendum A: Customer-Managed KMS & Network Exclusions" that carves out customer-controlled KMS and last-mile edge networking from Redwood uptime calculations, with the following constraints:
  * Redwood remains responsible for the Redwood-managed control plane, model-serving runtime, and peering we've provisioned into the customer's VPC.
  * Exclusions apply only when the incident's primary root cause is customer-controlled infra (KMS/HSM, customer's WAN/edge gateway).
  * For incidents involving multiple contributing factors, we propose a proportional attribution process (incident review with evidence provided by customer).

- Evidence: We will require timely logs and KMS error traces from your ops team for forensic attribution (timestamped KMS audit logs, egress flow traces, and traceroutes). We can accept redacted audit entries that include request IDs and timestamps.

- Availability target: We can support a 99.5% availability commitment for the Redwood-managed components under this addendum. Full-credit SLAs (99.9%/99.95%) remain available if the deployment uses Redwood-managed KMS or dedicated connectivity (we can discuss options).

I'm attaching a short draft (PDF) that legal can iterate on. Can your team confirm they can share the KMS audit slices and WAN flow logs on request? If yes, I'll loop in Legal for formal exception language.

Attachments: draft-sla-exception-proposal.pdf

Best,
Aditya Rao
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Dana Mills <dana@cyneris-health.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@cyneris-health.com
Date: Wed, 20 Oct 2027 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: SLA coverage for private deployment with customer-managed KMS

Aditya —

Thanks, that structure looks reasonable. We can provide KMS audit slices (request IDs+timestamps, encrypted key IDs) and short WAN flow logs for incident windows — security will redact B2C patient identifiers before sharing. A few clarifications:

1) Attribution timing — procurement wants the incident review window to be 30 days for producing logs/evidence. Is that acceptable?
2) Service credits — if the incident is attributed 100% to Redwood-managed components but the remediation required a KMS rotation on our side, will Redwood prorate credits once the rotation window is completed? We want predictable outcomes for mixed-cause incidents.
3) Monitoring — our SOC asks whether Redwood can surface Redwood-managed runtime health (per-route latency percentiles and token-rate metrics) into a read-only dashboard for 90 days post-incident so we can correlate with KMS logs.

If you can confirm the above we can greenlight procurement and legal will expect the first draft by Friday.

Dana

Team — forwarding Cyneris' reply and our draft. Procurement asked for a formal decision by EOD today; legal is on the thread but we need product/ops and legal sign-off on the exception mechanics. Summary of the ask:

- Approve: "SLA Addendum A" that excludes customer-managed KMS and last-mile WAN from Redwood uptime calculations, with a 99.5% availability target for Redwood-managed runtime.
- Requirements we must include in the addendum:
  1) Evidence requirements: customer-provided KMS audit slices and WAN flow logs within a 30-day production window; acceptance of redacted logs that include unique request IDs and timestamps.
  2) Attribution process: 3-person review (Redwood SRE + Redwood Legal + Customer ops) to determine root cause and apply proportional crediting for multi-cause incidents.
  3) Read-only telemetry: grant the customer 90-day read-only access to per-route latency and token-rate dashboards for post-incident correlation.
  4) Credit proration: if remediation requires customer action (e.g., KMS rotation) but the primary cause is Redwood-managed, Redwood will prorate credits after rotation window; legal to define exact mechanics.

I've attached the draft addendum PDF for legal redlines. If we approve this language today I will send to Cyneris and request their legal to sign. If you have changes, please mark them directly on the PDF and reply-all.

Quoting Cyneris' last message for context:

> > 3) Monitoring — our SOC asks whether Redwood can surface Redwood-managed runtime health (per-route latency percentiles and token-rate metrics) into a read-only dashboard for 90 days post-incident so we can correlate with KMS logs.

Next steps I propose: legal (Monica) takes the attached PDF, adds the exact wording for proration and the three-person review, Soojin confirms telemetry scope and ops-level acceptance, Marissa confirms commercial wording for credits and commit duration. If we can close today, I will send the addendum to Cyneris and open the DocuSign.

Thanks —
Aditya
